name: DENMARK
lead: Denmark is a small, flat country in northern Europe. Giant bridges link its islands. It gave the world LEGO, Vikings and Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tales. Danes love cycling and cosy candlelit evenings called hygge.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Denmark has the Jutland peninsula and over 400 islands. It is so flat that its highest hill is only 171 m. Sandy beaches, chalk cliffs and beech forests line the coasts.
The Great Belt Bridge is nearly 18 km long. The Øresund Bridge links Denmark to Sweden. You can drive between two countries over open sea in minutes.
animals: Harbour porpoises and grey seals swim along the coast. White storks nest on southern rooftops each spring. Red deer roam the old beech forests.
European hares sprint at 70 km/h across open fields. Each autumn, millions of starlings swirl in giant clouds over southern marshes. Danes call this 'Sort Sol', or Black Sun.
culture: Hygge means cosiness, warm company, candles and hot drinks. Smørrebrød are open sandwiches piled with herring, eggs or roast beef. People eat them with a knife and fork.
The name LEGO comes from 'leg godt', which means 'play well'. Denmark also gave us the storyteller Hans Christian Andersen. Danish design is famous for clean, simple shapes.
history: The Vikings sailed from Denmark over 1,000 years ago in longships. They reached England, Iceland, Greenland and even North America. Danish kings once ruled a vast northern empire.
Denmark became a peaceful constitutional monarchy in 1849. Today it is among the least corrupt nations. Education and healthcare are free.
wows: Legend says the Dannebrog, the oldest flag still in use, fell from the sky in 1219.
Denmark makes around 60% of its electricity from wind.
LEGO began in a tiny Danish carpentry workshop in 1932.
Copenhagen's cycle lanes carry more bikes than cars every day.
Greenland, the world's largest island, is part of the Danish realm.
Denmark is often among the world's happiest countries in the UN report.
Nowhere in Denmark is more than 52 km from the sea.

myths.myth: The Little Mermaid has a happy ending
myths.fact: In Andersen's tale, the mermaid turns into sea foam. She does not marry the prince.
Real Viking helmets were plain iron caps. Artists in the 1800s added horns for costumes and operas.
